Implementation Plan

PLAN: make `_is_gh_permanent_failure` stop retrying HTTP 400, HTTP 401, `Bad credentials` and `Requires authentication` (Refs #7355, local ID `gh-retry-auth-permanent`)

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-7355` at `53164c5918ba52d08ff7721acda4f8cd27b67dc6` (integration branch metadata `orchestrator/project-7355`; integration branch mismatch: false).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _is_gh_permanent_failure
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one regex extension plus a focused test and a changelog fragment, and it explicitly rules out other helpers, the attempt budget and generic 403. The one edit outside that list is a single line in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so the new test actually runs. Without it, `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` fails CI for any new `tests/test_*.py` that no workflow names. Updating the Python twin's mirror regex in `scripts/gh_api_retry.py` would cost about 3 lines, but the issue explicitly says not to touch any other helper. It is therefore left out and recorded as a known parity gap (D2), not done quietly. §6 order (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed) does not push past the requested scope here: the gap is only reachable on an unusual path where no status code is present, and it fails safe there (the Python path still retries).

### Automation / scheduler surface (§20.E)
- No new script and no new long-running supervisor. This only changes existing code: one line in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`, plus a test, a CI wiring line and a changelog fragment.
- Entry point: none new. The changed helper already runs inside every workflow that sources `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`. The new test runs in the existing `ci.yml` step "Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests (CLAUDE.md §15)" on `pull_request` and `push`.
- No database work. No entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`
- `tests/test_gh_retry_permanent_auth_failures.py`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-18-gh-retry-auth-permanent.md`

## Functions or modules to implement

1. `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`, `_is_gh_permanent_failure` (line 183). Same name, same signature (`$1` = text, returns 0 or 1).
   - Change the single `grep -qiE` pattern to add four alternatives: `HTTP 400`, `HTTP 401`, `Bad credentials`, `Requires authentication`. The resulting pattern:
     `"['\"][^'\"]+['\"] not found|gh: Not Found|HTTP 404|404 Not Found|status code 404|HTTP 400|HTTP 401|HTTP 422|Bad credentials|Requires authentication|Resource not accessible by (integration|personal access token)"`
   - Extend the doc comment's "Matches:" list (lines 167-182) with the four new items. Add one line saying generic `HTTP 403` is deliberately not matched: `gh_retry` and `gh_retry_to_file` check permanent failures before rate limits, and some 403s are secondary-rate-limit or content-creation throttles.
   - Do not touch `_is_gh_rate_limit`, `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, backoff, `_gh_api_classify` or any other function.

2. `tests/test_gh_retry_permanent_auth_failures.py` (new, pytest). Follow `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py`, which was studied as the representative:
   - Reuse its harness shape: the `FAKE_GH` bash stub that reads per-attempt files from `$FAKE_GH_PLAN/N.{stdout,stderr,rc}`, counts calls in `$FAKE_GH_PLAN/calls`, and answers `gh api -i /rate_limit` without spending an attempt.
   - Copy its `_setup(tmp_path, attempts)` env handling: drop `TG_BOT_SECRET`, `TG_ADMIN_CHAT_ID`, `TG_CHAT_ID` and `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS`; set `PATH`, `TMPDIR`, `GH_RATE_LIMIT_BREAKER_FILE` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`.
   - Copy `_run`: `set -uo pipefail; source scripts/gh_helpers.sh; sleep() { :; }; <body>`. Also copy `_calls`.
   - Copy the helpers into the new file rather than importing the other test module, because test modules are not a package API.
   - Test cases:
     a. `test_permanent_failure_matches_auth_and_bad_request` (parametrized). Pass each sample through an env var (`SAMPLE`) and run `_is_gh_permanent_failure "$SAMPLE"`; expect exit 0 for:
        - `HTTP 401: Bad credentials (https://api.github.com/user)`
        - `gh: Bad credentials (HTTP 401)`
        - `HTTP 400: Bad Request`
        - `gh: Requires authentication (HTTP 401)`
        - regression cases still true: `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` and `HTTP 422: Validation Failed`
     b. `test_permanent_failure_does_not_match_rate_limits_or_server_errors` (parametrized); expect non-zero for:
        - `HTTP 403: API rate limit exceeded for user ID 1.`
        - `You have exceeded a secondary rate limit`
        - `HTTP 502: Bad Gateway`
        - the unauthenticated rate-limit text `API rate limit exceeded for 203.0.113.7. (But here's the good news: Authenticated requests get a higher rate limit.)`, which guards against "Authenticated" being mistaken for "Requires authentication"
        - `error connecting to api.github.com`
     c. `test_gh_retry_makes_one_attempt_on_401`: stub plan `[("{\"message\":\"Bad credentials\"}", "gh: Bad credentials (HTTP 401)\n", 1)]`, body `gh_retry gh api /repos/o/r`. Assert rc != 0, `_calls == 1`, `non-retryable` in stderr, and empty stdout (failed body not replayed).
     d. `test_gh_retry_makes_one_attempt_on_400_and_requires_authentication` (parametrized over the two stderr samples): `_calls == 1`.
     e. `test_gh_retry_to_file_makes_one_attempt_on_401`: `gh_retry_to_file out.json gh api /repos/o/r`. Assert `_calls == 1`, rc != 0, and `out.json` empty or missing. This covers the second retry loop (line 1175) that the issue names.
     f. Control `test_gh_retry_still_retries_502`: run with `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`; assert `_calls == 3`. This proves the stub counts retries, so the single-attempt assertions mean something.
   - Use a GET (`gh api /repos/o/r`, no `-f`) so `_gh_cmd_is_unsafe_post` never forces `max_attempts=1` and hides the behaviour under test.

3. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: in the step "Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests (CLAUDE.md §15)" (around lines 1388-1402), add `tests/test_gh_retry_permanent_auth_failures.py \` next to `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py \`. Keep 2-space YAML indentation and the existing trailing-backslash list shape. Add a few words to the step comment about 400/401 being non-retryable. The file is about 105 KB, far below the 480,000-byte guard.

4. `changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-18-gh-retry-auth-permanent.md`: use the existing fragment shape (first line `<!-- changelog: changed -->`, then one bullet; see `changelog.d/6711-needs-human-digest.md`). The bullet should:
   - say `gh_retry` and `gh_retry_to_file` now stop after one attempt on HTTP 400, HTTP 401, `Bad credentials` and `Requires authentication`, instead of spending the full attempt budget (default 5, with backoff);
   - say generic HTTP 403 is deliberately still not treated as permanent, because secondary rate limits and content-creation throttles also answer 403 and permanent failures are checked before rate limits;
   - end with `Refs #7355.` and never use a closing keyword (§21).

## Data structures affected
None. No state, schema, label, marker or env var changes.

## API or interface changes
- `_is_gh_permanent_failure` now returns true for four more failure texts. Callers:
  - `gh_retry` and `gh_retry_to_file`: a 400 or 401 now fails after one attempt with the existing `::warning::gh command failed with non-retryable error` line, rc 1, and no sleep.
  - `_gh_api_classify` (line 861): only reached when status is empty, 403 or 429 and the text is not a rate limit. A status-less "Bad credentials" or "Requires authentication" text is now `permanent` instead of `transient`. This matches `gh_api_retry`'s documented rule that non-limit 4xx is permanent.
- Return codes, function names, log prefixes and env vars are unchanged.

## Decisions

### D1 — Literal alternatives, no generic 403
- Chosen: add `HTTP 400|HTTP 401|Bad credentials|Requires authentication` to the existing alternation, in the existing style (no word-boundary anchors, as with `HTTP 404`).
- Alternatives considered: add `HTTP 403` as the source doc proposed; anchor with `HTTP 40[01]([^0-9]|$)`.
- Why: both retry loops check permanent failures before rate limits, so a generic 403 would turn secondary-limit and content-creation 403s into immediate failures. That would be a correctness regression. Anchoring adds nothing, because GitHub never reports four-digit statuses, and the existing 404/422 alternatives are unanchored.

### D2 — Leave the Python twin's mirror regex unchanged
- Chosen: do not edit `_PERMANENT_TEXT_RE` in `scripts/gh_api_retry.py` (lines 64-67).
- Alternatives considered: mirror the four alternatives there and add parity cases to `tests/fixtures/gh_api_retry/classify_cases.json`.
- Why: the issue explicitly forbids changing any other helper. The divergence shows only when no status code can be read from stderr. Then bash `_gh_api_classify` says `permanent` and Python `classify` says `transient`, and the Python side just retries, which is the old behaviour (fails safe). No existing fixture case hits it, so `tests/test_gh_api_retry_py.py` and `tests/test_gh_api_retry.py` stay green. Recorded as a follow-up candidate.

### D3 — Wire the test into an existing CI step
- Chosen: add the file to "Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests (CLAUDE.md §15)".
- Alternatives considered: a new step or job; leaving it unwired.
- Why: `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` fails CI for unwired test files. agents.md says a new test goes into an existing step of the job that covers its topic, and that step already runs the sibling gh_helpers retry tests.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none added. The helper classifies stderr from `gh`, which can carry server text. The classification only reduces retries; it grants nothing. The `::warning::` stderr echo already escapes through `_
